solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Odd cola drunk outside foreign casino

indicators.note: outside says the first shuffled group wraps around the second
drunk suggests the letters of cola are reeling about into a new order
foreign suggests casino is made strange, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone downs a cola while standing outside a casino abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns COLA into OC...AL, which goes 'outside' CASION, the letters of CASINO rearranged as 'foreign' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occasional happens only now and then, as an odd event does.

clue.text: Hens — headless birds

indicators.note: headless says the first letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: hens are domestic fowls

explanation.surface: Chickens with their heads chopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes the F from FOWLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are a family of nocturnal birds of prey, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Chippy — go in after fish

indicators.note: after places the entering word behind the fish

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip shop customer heads inside after buying fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippy' looks like a British chip shop, but here it is the informal name for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a joiner or woodworker, a tradesman who works with timber.

clue.text: Prime Minister rises following second snooze

indicators.note: following says the reversed name comes after the abbreviation for second
rises in a down clue means the name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister gets up shortly after dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads the name upwards. Sir Robert Peel was a Victorian-era British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To snooze is to nap or doze, a short spell of slumber.

clue.text: Well-behaved soldier

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means tidy and disciplined
a soldier who attends an officer or carries orders

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for disciplined conduct and the name of an attendant soldier.

clue.text: A test almost supporting American country

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the following piece sits beneath the one before it

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: An American country is being tested, nearly passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TRIAL to TRIA, which in this down clue is 'supporting' US, written below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe, so it is a country.

clue.text: Shy drunkard comes back with son

indicators.note: comes back says the word for the drinker is read in reverse

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A timid drinker returns home with his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns SOT into TOS. 'Shy' looks like timid, but it is the verb meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy something is to fling it, as at a coconut shy, the same as a throw.

clue.text: Musical composition lifted from popular EP outrageously

indicators.note: lifted says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of music borrowed from a wildly popular extended-play record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the run concealed in 'popular EP outrageously'; 'lifted' in a down clue reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music, a large-scale composition.

clue.text: Gents swimming across river subsequently get tougher

indicators.note: across says the shuffled letters sit either side of the river
swimming suggests the letters of gents are moving around

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
subsequently means then, afterwards

explanation.surface: Men swim across a river and come out hardier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges GENTS to STENG, which goes 'across' R to give STRENG.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen is to make or become stronger, so tougher.

clue.text: Liberal Al Gore unfortunately missing start of outburst

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the name is mangled into another order
missing says one letter of the name is left out of the jumble
start of picks the first letter of outburst

explanation.surface: A liberal politician, Al Gore, sadly fails to have an outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AL GORE, less the O that starts 'outburst' ('missing'), are rearranged as 'unfortunately' signals. 'Liberal' looks like a party label but means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal and large both mean generous or ample, as in a large helping.

clue.text: Leave Detective Inspector with article in private

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector

indicators.note: in says the article sits inside the soldier word

parts.note: a sapper is a private soldier in the Royal Engineers
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A detective leaves with a newspaper article in confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like secret, but it is a rank-and-file soldier, a SAPPER, which takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish or go away, so to leave.

clue.text: Unattractively artificial end in picture

indicators.note: in says the word for end goes inside the short word for picture

parts.note: pic is short for picture
the last is the end

explanation.surface: An ugly, fake ending to a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is used of things that look cheap and fake, such as a plastic smile.

clue.text: Caesar perhaps appears regularly in troubled Rome

indicators.note: in says the picked letters go inside the jumbled city
troubled suggests Rome is thrown into disorder, its letters rearranged
regularly picks every other letter of appears

explanation.surface: Caesar turns up from time to time in a strife-torn Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesar perhaps' names an example, not the man himself; 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'appears', and 'troubled' scrambles the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Caesars were Roman rulers, so a Caesar is an example of an imperial ruler; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: A drink around middle of day? Another time

indicators.note: around says the spirit wraps the central letter

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of day

explanation.surface: A midday drink, and then once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, on another occasion.

clue.text: Materials from underwater vessels in position? On the contrary

indicators.note: in on its own would put the vessels inside the position
On the contrary reverses the containment, so the position goes inside the vessels instead

parts.note: subs are submarines
a stance is a position

explanation.surface: Asks whether substances come from submarines at their stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' is a setter's way of flipping the order the clue's words imply, so the container and contents swap roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances are kinds of matter, so materials in the general sense.

clue.text: Left with last bit of dignity after madman loses head completely

indicators.note: after says the madman piece comes before the other letters
loses head says the first letter of the slang word is dropped

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of dignity

explanation.surface: Someone loses all dignity entirely after a lunatic goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like part of the madman's story but is the abbreviation L; 'nutter' is British slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly means totally, to the fullest degree, so completely.

clue.text: List of military personnel includes old bird

indicators.note: includes says the duty list takes the letter inside

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties, originally military

explanation.surface: A duty roster names an aged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel, so a bird.

clue.text: Trial: a time to persuade

parts.note: to tempt is to entice or persuade

explanation.surface: A trial is a chance to talk someone round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like a court case but means a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a try or effort, the same as an attempt.

clue.text: Weird shout came — Poirot devoted a lot of time to it

definitions.text: Poirot devoted a lot of time to it

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of shout came are strangely jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd cry rang out about Poirot's grooming habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercule Poirot, Agatha Christie's Belgian detective, is famed for fussing over his waxed facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Poirot spends long hours tending his upper-lip hair, so the description points to that whisker growth.

clue.text: Grave debts following end of dealings with the Queen

indicators.note: following says the debts come behind the other letters
end of picks the final letter of dealings

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Debts left by the Queen's financial dealings are no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means solemn or weighty, as a serious matter is.

clue.text: We rest a high jumper

indicators.note: high, like drunk, suggests the letters are in an altered state and rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete in the high jump takes a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'high jumper' an athlete; split it, and 'high' is the anagram signal while 'jumper' is the British word for a knitted top.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a jumper is a knitted pullover, the same garment as a sweater.

clue.text: Add in evidence about daughter

indicators.note: about says the evidence word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a clue is a piece of evidence
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone adds evidence about a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add in' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Add' and IN is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something is to add it to a group or set.

clue.text: One caught diving bird coming up for something to eat?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the bird is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the grebe is a diving waterbird

explanation.surface: A diving bird is caught and surfaces with a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns GREBE into EBERG. The question mark warns the definition is oblique: an iceberg lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a crisp variety of lettuce, so it is an edible salad leaf.

clue.text: A carriage returns separately

indicators.note: returns says the carriage word is read backwards

parts.note: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A coach goes back on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TRAP into PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means set aside or individually, so separately.

clue.text: Fish's point of view

definitions.meaning: to fish with rod and line

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to go fishing with a rod and a slant or perspective.

clue.text: Polished end of table leg — walnut — regularly

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of table

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of walnut

explanation.surface: Describes a well-finished walnut table leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of walnut, ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means refined and stylish, which is what polished conveys.

clue.text: At least 18 heads of Academies denounced unsatisfactory, lazy teachers

indicators.note: heads of picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Academy principals, at least eighteen of them, condemn idle staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At least 18' reads as a count of heads, but it is the definition: the age of majority.
explanation.definitionFit: In most places a person aged eighteen or over is legally a grown-up.

clue.text: A place to eat hash

definitions.meaning: a dining room for service personnel
to make a hash of something is to make a muddle of it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military dining hall and a muddle or botch.

clue.text: Tiger ate nuts after initially cutting snout

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters come behind the first letter
initially picks the first letter of cutting
nuts suggests the letters of tiger ate go crazy, into a new order

explanation.surface: A deranged tiger ate after first biting off an animal's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snout' looks like a nose but is British prison slang for tobacco, here a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is British slang for tobacco or a single smoke, a rolled tobacco stick.

clue.text: Article taken from dirty relative

indicators.note: taken from says the article is removed from the synonym

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story lifted from a grubby family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, so a relative.

clue.text: Tramp covered in waste paper

indicators.note: covered in says the letters sit concealed within the phrase

explanation.surface: A vagrant buried in rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant, but it is the verb, to tread.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to tread heavily, to walk step after step.

clue.text: Intelligence shown by bishop with correct cape

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
right means correct
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A clever bishop is shown wearing the right cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment but is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightness can mean cleverness or quick wit, a sense of intelligence.
